title: One evaluated strict projection with a perfect quotient
statement: Let X,Y be small sites and f a geometric inverse image with its canonical constant coefficient lift [def-pur-adic-site-strict-quotient-interface]. For a commutative ring A, ideal I, positive quotient index n and F in the ordinary unbounded derived module category on X, suppose the A-module A/I^(n+1), placed in degree zero, is perfect [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Then evaluation at n of the canonical strict counit projection reduction_Y(Rf_* F) to Rf_*^J(reduction_X F) is an isomorphism. Only this coefficient level is assumed perfect; A need not be Noetherian. The reductions, evaluation and projection are exactly the normalized scalar quotient constructions of the cited interface.

source.place: Tag 0944 (lemma-projection-formula), equation 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map), Tags 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), 07A6 (lemma-adjoint) and 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok); one coefficient-level projection and its strict evaluation.

proof.text: Choose a bounded finite-projective representative of A/I^(n+1), split every term off a finite free module, and apply exact constant realization to its representative and splitting equations. This makes the constant quotient a perfect coefficient, including the zero quotient.

source.place: Tag 0944, perfect coefficient hypothesis; Modules on Sites Tag 03EI.

proof.text: Evaluation of the scalar quotient reduction on a flat-term K-flat representative is derived tensor with the constant quotient. The ordinary comparison is the identity on pure tensors. The full cochain normalization of reductionPullIso and the counit normalization of evaluatePushIso identify the evaluated towerProjection with the canonical counit-defined tensor projection after the endpoint isomorphisms.

Apply the perfect-coefficient projection formula and conjugate by these endpoint isomorphisms. The input may be unbounded; the bound belongs solely to the coefficient. No flatness of the quotient or uniform bound on levels is needed.

theorem perfectReductionProjectionEvaluation (n : ℕ)
    (hperfect : letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard (ModuleCat.{u} A)
      DerivedCategory.IsPerfectRingComplex
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj
          (ModuleCat.of A (quotientRing A I n)))) (F : X.derived A) :
    IsIso ((Y.evaluate A n).map (f.towerProjection A I F))
